expectations.text: Selects external, LH, conventional without reversing an internal program by hand.
expectations.evidence: Findings: 'Only the qualitative spec is known: external M8x1, left-hand, conventional milling, 6 mm thread length...'; 'The M2.5 fixture in the repo is unrelated regression evidence for a different (internal, RH) thread and must not be reused as a stand-in for this cutter's geometry or this thread's programmed diameters.' No hand-mirroring/reversal is proposed anywhere.

expectations.text: Requires cutting OD and axial configuration independently of shank marking and flute count.
expectations.evidence: Findings: 'in vendor thread-mill designations "D4" is typically the shank diameter and "50L" the overall length... "triple flute" is a circumferential-edge count, independent of the number of axial thread forms'; Q1 asks cutting/thread-form OD and Q2 asks 'effective cutting length / number of axial thread forms... Triple-flute alone does not establish any of these' as a separate item.

expectations.text: Reviews the entire exterior orbit, neck/shank/holder and shoulder/runout, including nearby clamps.
expectations.evidence: Q4: 'checked as an obstacle for the cutter, neck, shank and holder through the whole orbit, lead-in/out and withdrawal — not just at the deepest pass'; Step 11 review re-confirms 'the deepest cutting point clears the measured shoulder height... the whole route including the first XY move... clears the motion floor, any landmarks and the clamp's stated extent'; Readiness item 6 restates 'tool orbit, entry, every radial pass, deepest cut point, shoulder and clamp clearance'.

expectations.text: Does not reuse an internal (major minus cutter)/2 orbit formula as an external recipe.
expectations.evidence: Findings: 'The M2.5 fixture... must not be reused as a stand-in for this cutter's geometry or this thread's programmed diameters.' No orbit-radius formula (internal or external) is invented anywhere in the plan; all radii are deferred to the operator-confirmed generator export.

expectations.text: Keeps all unknown generator fields pending and issues no motion or staging.
expectations.evidence: Steps 1-5 are read-only (get_connection_status/get_position/get_stored_state/get_machine_profile/get_tool_setter_config); step 6 is the single batched 9-question message [WAIT]; 'Counts: logical approvals = ... ' section confirms no approval is staged in this turn; the tool-change and submission steps are all explicitly gated behind '(After the answers land.)' / 'Only if the operator then explicitly requests execution'.

stated_logical_approvals: Plan states 'logical approvals = 1 tool change x 4 + 1 feature job = 5 (+1 more, a probe_program datum measurement, only if Q8's answer says the boss WCS is not yet established)' and separately 'literal [APPROVAL] tags in Steps = 5'. Actual literal count of [APPROVAL]-tagged steps in the Steps section is 6 (lines with run_tool_setter x2, goto_tool_change_position, apply_tool_length_offset, the conditional probe_program, and submit_gcode_job) — the plan's own literal-tag figure (5) undercounts by 1 against its own text; its logical-approval figure (5, +1 conditional) matches the 6 literal tags once the conditional one is included.

claims.claim: tool_length_applied cannot be honestly declared until the tool-change flow (step 8) has actually run and been verified.
claims.evidence: Readiness: 'tool_length_applied: true requires the tool-change flow (step 8) to have actually run and been verified against a reliable position — right now the fitted tool is the touch probe, not the thread mill.' Correct per tool-change skill's flow-A sequencing.

claims.claim: A preflight recheck immediately before submission is a second legitimate 'ask once' batch, distinct from the setup question batch.
claims.evidence: Critique itself flags this as a guess: 'nothing states explicitly that a second batched question is permitted this way... I guessed that the preflight recheck is a legitimate second "ask once" round.' Plausible but not confirmed against the skill text; correctly self-flagged as unverified rather than presented as fact.

uncertainties: Whether triple-flute designs conventionally correspond to a single axial row — explicitly left unresolved and asked rather than assumed.
Which mechanism (set_landmark vs a probe_program keep-out) is correct for representing an unmeasured clamp.

suggestions.reason: Sonnet's own stated 'literal [APPROVAL] tags = 5' does not match the 6 tags actually present in its Steps section (the conditional probe_program tag at step 9 is text-present but excluded from its own count). This is a self-consistency defect the eval's assertions don't check for eval 3, worth a generic cross-eval assertion: 'the plan's stated literal tag count matches the tags actually present.'

eval_feedback.overall: All 5 assertions pass with concrete, specific evidence. Sonnet's depth on shoulder/plunge-column geometry is noticeably shallower than opus's (no tooth-to-tip or plunge-column collision reasoning), but the assertions as written do not require that level of detail, so this does not affect the grade.
